And those who were found alive

And in the year 1491 [AG],
[1491] Manuel, king of the Greeks, fell ill.
And when he perceived that he was dying,
he became a monk,
and set the crown upon his son Alexios,
whom he proclaimed king.
And his wife, that is, the mother of the youth Alexios, he made a nun,
and entrusted to her the affairs of the kingdom.
And they appointed twelve grandees
to command the armies.
Now that nun-queen,
after a short time, fell into adultery with one of the twelve grandees.
And when the rest desired
to depose her and her son,
and to set up the daughter of Manuel who was from his first wife,
and to proclaim her husband king,
they were not able [to do so].
For the conspiracy {OCR?} was revealed,
and those grandees were afraid and fled to the Great Church [Hagia Sophia].
And there was battle in the city for seven days,
and much blood was shed in Constantinople itself,
and those with the king and his mother set up catapults against Hagia Sophia.
Then Theodosius, their patriarch,
when the king and his mother swore to him that they would not harm those in the church if they came out,
went in to them,
and on his guarantee brought them out.
The king and his mother, however, trampled on their oaths,
and blinded the eyes of those eleven,
and killed their followers.
Then the patriarch, being utterly distressed,
excommunicated the whole city,
and abandoned it and departed to a monastery outside,
and suspended the church bell and prayer for nine months.
And with the burial of a donkey,
without a funeral procession,
their dead were being buried.
And in that same year, Sultan Qilij Arslan sent an army against Ra'ban,
and an army of the Damascenes came against them,
and the Cappadocians fled;
for they were already much worn out by the wars with the Franks.
And in this same year, which is the year 575
[575] of the Arabs, the Caliph al-Mustadi died,
and in his place arose his son al-Nasir.
After ... {OCR?} his son [reigned] forty-seven years.
When this one arose,
he seized the vizier Ibn al-Attar and imprisoned him,
and threw him into irons,
and took everything that he possessed.
